title: The Chinese dynasties
query:
#! title: The Chinese dynasties
#! lane: china
#! asks: Which dynasty was ruling China
#! verb: begin
#! past: began
#! kind: reigns
#! source: Wikidata
#! licence: CC0 1.0
#! url: https://query.wikidata.org/

# The twelve dynasties a reader means when they ask what order the Chinese
# dynasties came in. The DATES are Wikidata's; the SELECTION is ours, and it
# is listed here rather than hidden in code so it can be argued with.
#
# Why a hand-picked list and not a class query: asking for everything typed as
# a "Chinese dynasty" returns 31 rows that leave out Qin, Sui, Yuan, Ming and
# Qing — they are typed as "historical Chinese state" instead — while
# including a dozen splinter dynasties of the Southern and Northern courts.
# Neither set is the sequence anyone is trying to learn.
#
# What this list does not show: the long stretches when China was not one
# state. Between the Han and the Sui, and again between the Tang and the Song,
# several dynasties ruled at once. The gaps between these rows are those
# centuries, and the app's questions say so rather than pretending to a clean
# baton-pass.
#
# Dates before 1 CE arrive negative and are printed BCE. They are also the
# place where Wikidata and the textbooks differ by a year or two (the Qin here
# begin in 220 BCE; most books say 221), which is why nothing built from this
# list asks for an exact year before 1000 CE — only for order.

SELECT ?item ?name ?from ?to WHERE {
  VALUES ?item {
    wd:Q169705   # Xia
    wd:Q128938   # Shang
    wd:Q35216    # Zhou
    wd:Q7183     # Qin
    wd:Q7209     # Han
    wd:Q7352     # Jin (266-420)
    wd:Q7405     # Sui
    wd:Q9683     # Tang
    wd:Q7462     # Song
    wd:Q7313     # Yuan
    wd:Q9903     # Ming
    wd:Q8733     # Qing
  }
  ?item wdt:P571 ?from .
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P576 ?to }
  ?item rdfs:label ?name . FILTER(LANG(?name) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?from
